notes: The demo's projects, drawn into folders by demo/build.py (pictures by demo/paint.py, one .docx description each). Everything is made up: the artist, the works, the places, the photographers. A work's file name carries its title, medium and size; an exhibition folder's name carries its year and town, and each photo's name its photographer and venue (sources/image_meta.py). 'views' lists, per installation photo, the works hung in it by index; 'details' the works shown close up.

projects.name: Low Tide
description: Low Tide is a series of paintings of one stretch of shore, made over a year of walks at the same hour. Each canvas starts from a drawing made on site and is finished in the studio from memory, so the bands of water, sand and sky are less a view than a record of how the place felt that morning.

The paintings are built in thin layers of oil, scraped back and painted again, the way the tide leaves and covers the same ground. Colour follows the season: grey and violet in winter, chalky greens in spring, the warm pinks of late summer evenings.
The series was first shown at Gallery One in Eastmoor in 2024, hung in the order the paintings were made, with the walking notes printed on a single sheet at the entrance.

projects.name: Paper Maps
description: Paper Maps are drawings of places drawn from memory and then corrected on foot. Each sheet begins as a map of somewhere familiar, a station, a market, a school yard, made at the kitchen table without looking anything up.

The artist then walks the place with the drawing and adds what was missing in a second ink, so every map shows two things at once: the place as it was remembered and the place as it is. The gaps between the two are left visible.
The drawings were shown at Museum Four in Northbay in 2023, framed simply and hung in a single line at eye height.

projects.name: Woven Weather
description: Woven Weather is a set of tapestries, each recording the weather of one day. Every row of the weave stands for an hour: its colour comes from the sky, its thickness from the wind, and a row is left loose when it rained.
The wool is dyed by hand with plants gathered near the studio, so the palette changes with the seasons in the same way the weather does. A day takes about a month to weave.
The tapestries were shown at Art Hall Two in Westfield in 2025, with the weather records for each day printed beside them.

works.title: Weather, 30 June
works.medium: Hand-woven wool and linen, plant dyes

projects.name: Rooms
description: Rooms is a series of small paintings of rooms seen through doorways: a kitchen at night, a hallway, a room kept for guests. No furniture is painted, only the colours of the walls and the light between them.
Each panel is painted from a photograph of a real room and then simplified until only the nested rectangles of doors and walls remain. The soft edges come from sanding the acrylic between layers.
The paintings were shown at Club Three in Eastmoor in 2022, in a narrow corridor so that visitors saw them one at a time.
